chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام that he said:
"Providing ifṭār to your fasting brother is more virtuous than your own fasting."

key_terms.أَخَاكَ: your brother, meaning a fellow believer
key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: more virtuous or superior in merit
key_terms.تَفْطِيرُكَ: your act of giving ifṭār or feeding someone to break the fast

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of providing ifṭār to a fasting person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the great virtue of feeding a fasting believer at the time of ifṭār. It highlights that serving others and strengthening bonds among believers can carry a reward even greater than one’s own voluntary act of fasting.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1954 - Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Abu al-Hasan (as) that he said:
"Providing iftar to your fasting brother is more virtuous than your own fasting."
